what_its_for: This combination medicine is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). It contains two medicines that work together: irbesartan (an ARB) relaxes your blood vessels so your heart does not have to work as hard, and hydrochlorothiazide (a water pill or diuretic) helps your kidneys remove extra salt and water from your body. Together, they lower your blood pressure and reduce your risk of heart attack, stroke, and kidney problems.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth once a day, with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Try to take it at the same time every day so it becomes part of your routine. Do not crush, chew, or split the tablet unless your pharmacist tells you it is safe to do so. Because this medicine contains a water pill, you may urinate more often, especially in the first few weeks. Try to take it in the morning so this does not disturb your sleep at night.
dosing: The usual starting dose is one tablet of irbesartan 150 mg / hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg once daily. Your doctor may increase your dose to irbesartan 300 mg / hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg or 300 mg / 25 mg once daily depending on how well your blood pressure is controlled. Always take the dose your doctor prescribed. Do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your pharmacist or doctor.
storage: Store this medicine at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C and 30°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medicine in its original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of unused or expired medicine safely — ask your pharmacist about a medicine take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid alcohol while taking this medicine, as it can lower your blood pressure further and make you feel dizzy or faint. Do not use potassium supplements or salt substitutes that contain potassium without talking to your doctor first, as this can affect your potassium levels. Avoid prolonged exposure to heat or becoming dehydrated (such as during intense exercise or hot weather), as this can cause your blood pressure to drop too low. Avoid taking other blood pressure medicines, NSAIDs (like ibuprofen or naproxen), or any new prescription or over-the-counter medicines without first checking with your doctor or pharmacist. Do not stop taking this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat (signs of a serious allergic reaction called angioedema); severe dizziness, fainting, or lightheadedness; decreased urination or signs of kidney problems; muscle cramps, weakness, or irregular heartbeat (which may be signs of electrolyte imbalance); signs of too much sun sensitivity such as a severe sunburn or rash; yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice); unusual bleeding or bruising; or if you become pregnant. Also contact your doctor if your blood pressure readings remain high, if you have persistent dry cough, or if you notice any new or worsening symptoms.
when_it_works: You may start to see a small drop in your blood pressure within the first 1 to 2 weeks of treatment. However, it may take up to 4 weeks to get the full benefit of this medicine. Keep taking it every day even if you feel well — high blood pressure often has no symptoms. Do not stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor, even if your blood pressure feels normal.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Do NOT take this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. It can seriously harm or cause death to an unborn baby, especially during the second and third trimesters. Tell your doctor right away if you become pregnant while taking this medicine. Breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding, as this medicine may pass into breast milk. Elderly patients: Older adults may be more sensitive to dizziness and low blood pressure with this medicine. Use caution when standing up quickly to avoid falls. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease, as your dose may need to be adjusted or this medicine may not be right for you. Children: This medicine is not approved for use in children under 18 years of age.
